answer: Stop sybils with a tundra harbor glacier: an agent bonds one harbor berth. Each cycle it cuts one glacier block from the tundra face and floats it in; verifiers match the block's melt line to the berth chart, voiding copies, slashing the bond. Forging 1,000 needs 1,000 berths at 18x: one block melts once at one harbor, its line set by that ice, unrepeatable at a second, cannot be copied, shared or bulk-bought. Honest agents cut once, keep rights.
